propositions: Four call sites use cast() to access optional capability members (add_comment, set_relationship) without runtime guards, allowing silent AttributeError swallows inside broad exception handlers when capabilities are absent

The reconciler is inconsistent with itself: dispatch_one and dispatch_apply_phases cast capability members without isinstance/hasattr checks, while fetcher.py gates the same capabilities with hasattr before access

A non-capable transport backend (Data Center) would fail silently when mutations are skipped inside except blocks, conflating designed skip with real failures and breaking observability into the reconciliation outcome
Runtime isinstance guards with distinct audit logging (capability-absent vs capability-present-but-raised) must replace static casts at four call sites to enable backend-agnostic capability dispatch
The isinstance check in Python 3.12+ uses getattr_static and fails on proxied __getattr__ transports, requiring a fallback to hasattr for correctness across Python 3.11+ version matrix
